workflow_pattern: This is a 'F3_collab_workflow_heavy' style workflow. It requires the following operations, in roughly this order: create repository, collaborator branch convention, add readme with content, copy external file to branch, create pull request, create workflow conditional comment by label, validate automation with test issues. The task should combine these operations into one coherent, realistic request without listing them as separate steps.
question:
Hello! I'm Ravi, a software engineer working on a voice-assistant hub with my teammate Zoe. I need your help creating a repository called voice-assistant-hub for our collaboration. Our workflow will be structured around a main branch for production-ready code and dedicated development branches: dev-ravi and dev-zoe. Please initialize the README.md file on main with: "# Voice Assistant Hub

A hub for building and testing wake-word detection and voice-command pipelines." For the initial setup, I'll be responsible for integrating porcupine_engine.py from picovoice's porcupine repository into my development branch, while Zoe will handle copying vad_utils.py from snakers4's silero-vad repository into her branch, given her expertise in voice activity detection. Following this setup, I'd like to create a pull request from dev-ravi to main with the title "Add wake-word engine integration" and description "This PR integrates the wake-word engine as the entry point for the voice assistant pipeline." We also need to implement an automation system that monitors newly created GitHub issues and responds with appropriate comments: issues labeled bug should receive the comment "Thank you. We will fix it.", issues labeled feature should get "Thank you, we will consider to include this feature.", and issues labeled discussion should get "Thanks for starting this discussion! We welcome community input." To validate this functionality, please create three test issues with the titles "Bug in wake-word detection" (with label bug), "Feature: multi-language support" (with label feature), and "Discussion: privacy concerns with always-on mic" (with label discussion), each with the corresponding labels.
